claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain in refractory high- or medium-entropy alloys is primarily governed by activation of edge-dislocation slip.
High-temperature toughness in these alloys is primarily governed by activation of edge-dislocation slip.
Nanoscale chemically ordered regions, such as B2-like phases, enhance edge-dislocation slip.
Nanoscale ordered regions lower local migration barriers for dislocation climb.
Nanoscale ordered regions promote a more homogeneous high-temperature strain distribution.
Ordering-induced homogeneous deformation improves toughness without unduly compromising strength.
Relevant refractory alloys can have a predominantly disordered single-phase BCC or FCC initial state.
Rapid solidification or minimal processing produces such a disordered state with limited pre-existing chemical ordering.
A controlled annealing treatment can induce fine nanoscale B2-type or other ordered precipitates without substantially changing overall composition.
Nanoscale precipitates can occur within a disordered BCC refractory high-entropy-alloy matrix.
The nanoscale precipitates relevant to the hypothesis are chemically ordered and mediate edge-dislocation motion.
At high temperature, local diffusion enables formation of nanoscale ordered regions.
Ordered regions facilitate both edge-dislocation glide and climb.
More uniform plastic strain delays localized failure and crack initiation.
Relative to a disordered baseline, induced nanoscale ordering will increase high-temperature ductility or plastic strain.
Relative to a disordered baseline, induced nanoscale ordering will improve fracture toughness.
Relative to a disordered baseline, induced nanoscale ordering will enhance edge-dislocation mobility and produce more uniform dislocation spacing.
The proposed effect holds at approximately 600–900 °C when diffusion is active but deleterious precipitate coarsening is avoided.
The qualitative role of chemical ordering in promoting edge-dislocation-mediated plasticity is supported by recent studies.

contradictions.description: The initial state is specified as single-phase BCC or FCC, whereas the baseline definition also permits a dual-phase state, so the intended control microstructure is not consistently defined.
